jobs.description:
We are looking for an experienced Lead QA Engineer to own quality for the Net2Phone billing platform. We are building a billing system where every invoice is provably correctly rated, taxed, prorated, reconciled and where the team can defend that claim with documented coverage rather than assumptions.

You will focus on testing billing correctness end-to-end: how a call becomes a rated record and then an invoice line, where usage gets lost or double-counted between the switch and the bill, how proration behaves when a customer changes plans mid-cycle, and how a third-party tax engine's output is verified when you can't inspect it. You are equally skilled in leading a team: setting the documentation standard, acting as the intake gatekeeper with Product, and deciding where automation effort yields true value.

This is a manual-testing-heavy position: automation leadership here means planning, prioritization, and coverage governance, not day-to-day framework development. You will not be the primary implementer, but you will be expected to read, review, and debug the team's suites.

  • PLEASE SUBMIT CV IN ENGLISH.
  • ONLY ACCEPTING CANDIDATES FROM LATAM.
  • ADVANCED SPOKEN ENGLISH IS REQUIRED.

Responsibilities

    • Act as an active member of a Scrum team, participating fully in all agile ceremonies and maintaining all related artifacts.

    • Own the test strategy for billing: Covering rating, mediation, invoicing, taxation, payments, credits, adjustments, dunning, and reseller/white-label billing hierarchies.

    • Design and document test coverage for month-end billing cycles, including cutoff and timezone boundaries, reruns, partial failures, and retry safety.

    • Perform revenue-assurance testing: Reconciling CDR volumes against invoiced amounts and quantifying the financial impact of any discrepancies.

    • Trace billing discrepancies to their root cause: Distinguishing rating-engine defects from mediation or switch-side issues, including reading SIP traces or packet captures when necessary.

    • Enforce the requirement intake gate: Ensuring no user story enters a sprint without testable acceptance criteria.

    • Set and enforce documentation standards: Ensuring requirement-to-test-case traceability and reviewable per-epic coverage.

    • Drive the automation roadmap: Deciding what gets automated, in what order, and with what expected ROI, while conducting code and test reviews for the resulting suites.

    • Establish and report billing quality metrics: Defect escape rate, coverage, defect density, and release readiness.

    • Mentor billing QA engineers and provide clear technical direction.

    • Communicate and escalate product quality risks: Holding ground when supported by data.

Requirements:

  • 8+ years in QA, including hands-on experience with a production billing, rating, or payments system.

  • Working knowledge of rating and usage billing: Rate decks, prefix matching, billing increments, minimum durations, connection fees, and destination zones.

  • Subscription billing experience: Recurring and non-recurring charges, mid-cycle proration, upgrades, downgrades, trials, promotions, and discounts.

  • Invoicing experience: Invoice generation, line-item totals, usage detail, credit memos, manual adjustments, refunds, and dunning.

  • Strong SQL skills (joins, aggregations, window functions) sufficient to reconcile usage against invoices independently.

  • Precision and rounding literacy: Decimal vs. floating-point representation, rounding modes, line-level vs. invoice-level rounding, and identifying where each produces cent-level defects.

  • Proven experience leading or mentoring QA engineers.

  • A track record of pushing back with evidence: Rejecting untestable requirements, holding releases based on data, and negotiating scope using metrics.

  • Proficiency with a formal Test Management System (TMS) and Jira.

  • Professional English proficiency (spoken and written) with reliable overlap with US Eastern business hours

We use the following technologies:

  • Python & Pytest: For service and integration automation.

  • Playwright: For UI automation.

  • SQL: For billing and rating data validation—this is a daily tool in this role, not an occasional one.

  • Allure TestOps: As our Test Management System (TMS). Automated test cases are linked to TMS cases, and we expect QA to extend coverage directly within it.

  • Jira: For project management and defect tracking.

  • GitHub Actions (GHA) & Jenkins: For CI/CD, leveraging shared pipeline libraries.

  • Grafana: For monitoring quality and delivery metrics, including defect escape rate.

  • Third-Party Tax Engine: For telecom tax and regulatory fee calculations.

    • We are always open to adopting any reasonable tool that drives higher quality into the product.

Pluses:

  • Working knowledge of SIP/VoIP call flows as they relate to billable records: call legs, answered vs. unanswered calls, billable vs. elapsed duration, transfers, and conference legs.

  • Proficiency in Python/pytest and Playwright: Valued for reviewing, debugging, and evaluating test automation, rather than building frameworks from scratch.

  • REST API testing experience against billing and rating services.

  • Payment gateway integration testing experience.

  • Telecom tax engine validation (Avalara, SureTax, Vertex, or equivalent).

  • Multi-currency and FX (foreign exchange) handling experience.

  • Familiarity with Jenkins and GitHub Actions (GHA) pipelines, sufficient to analyze and interpret build results.

We are pleased to offer:

  • Remote work opportunity!

  • B2B Employment ($, gross).

  • Stable job with long-term growth perspective.

  • Competitive salary with annual performance review.

  • Really good hardware.

  • An exciting and challenging job with talented people around.

  • Continuous learning and career growth opportunities.

  • Compensation for professional training, seminars, and conferences.

  • Referral program: get rewarded for helping us grow the team with talented people.

  • Company-supported English classes to enhance your professional growth.

About us:

IDT Technologies is a part of IDT Corporation—an American telecommunications company founded in 1990 and headquartered in New Jersey. It is an industry leader in prepaid communication and payment services and one of the world's largest international voice carriers. We are listed on the NYSE, employ over 1,500 people across 20+ countries, and have revenues in excess of $1.5 billion.

Net2Phone () is a global provider of unified cloud communications solutions. It offers an integrated communications suite featuring powerful collaboration tools, including voice, messaging, chat, and unlimited domestic and international calling to 23+ countries.

Claroty is a global leader in cyber-physical systems (CPS) protection, dedicated to securing the critical infrastructure that keeps the world running. We’re a fast-growing, award-winning team where innovation meets purpose—and we want you to help us define the future of cybersecurity.

﻿As a Solutions Engineer at Claroty, you will serve as a strategic technical advisor and trusted partner throughout the sales lifecycle. You will bridge business needs with deep technical expertise, supporting enterprise customers across industrial, healthcare, energy, and critical infrastructure sectors.

In this high-impact, customer-facing role, you will collaborate closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to design and deliver tailored cybersecurity solutions that protect complex OT/ICS environments.   • Represent Claroty at industry conferences, trade shows, and customer events. Lead webinars and contribute to technical content, strengthening Claroty’s reputation as a leader in OT cybersecurity.
  • Leverage internal and public generative AI tools (e.g., Gemini, specialized technical bots, and automated RFP platforms) to accelerate prospect research, aggregate business intelligence, and streamline documentation- maximizing your time spent on high-value technical strategy and solution architecture.

Requirements

  • 5+ years in Sales Engineering, Solutions Architecture, or a similar customer-facing technical role, preferably within cybersecurity, industrial automation, networking, or enterprise SaaS
  • Expert-level L2–L4 troubleshooting. Mastery of traffic acquisition (SPAN/RSPAN, TAPs, virtual switching) and virtualization (VMware, Hyper-V).
  • Deep knowledge of industrial protocols (Modbus, CIP, DNP3, IEC 61850) and architect-level understanding of the Purdue Model.

The AI-powered Claroty Platform serves as the single source of operational truth, providing the deepest visibility and broadest protection across cyber-physical systems (CPS), leveraging five core solutions: asset inventory, exposure management, network protection, secure access, and threat detection. Claroty helps organizations operationalize CPS protection through a programmatic approach designed to reduce risk, maintain operational integrity, and meet compliance–whether in the cloud with Claroty xDome or on-premise with Claroty Continuous Threat Detection (CTD). Claroty is deployed by hundreds of organizations at thousands of sites globally. The company is headquartered in New York City and has a presence in Europe, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America. To learn more, visit claroty.com.

Claroty is widely recognized as the industry leader in CPS protection, backed by the world’s largest investment firms and industrial automation vendors. The company has been named a Leader in 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for CPS Protection Platforms two years in a row, a Customers’ Choice in the 2026 Gartner® Peer Insights™ Voice of the Customer for CPS Protection Platforms, and a Leader and a Customer Favorite in The Forrester Wave™: Operational Technology Security Solutions, Q3 2026. The Opportunity:

Our goal is to make Grafana the single best place where humans and AI agents understand and act on real-time data from across the enterprise. As part of this initiative, we are building an AI-native data intelligence system that gives agents reliable, governed access to enterprise context. This system helps agents retrieve the right data, metadata, definitions, lineage, quality signals, and institutional knowledge without every agent builder having to maintain their own brittle context files. The principle is simple: the context system retrieves, agents decide, and data teams maintain the intelligence.

Engineers are empowered to make decisions, move quickly, and validate ideas early – while being supported by a deeply collaborative culture that values curiosity, feedback, and cross-functional partnership.

We are a remote-first team that meets regularly over video and does most of our work asynchronously, in writing. We value creativity, diverse perspectives, and clear communication. Tempo is relied upon by prominent global organizations to monitor critical applications and infrastructure, and we expect everyone on the team, including our Staff engineers, to contribute ideas that make it a more reliable, more useful, and more loved product.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Contracts Specialist
Reports to: Finance Lead
Location: Herndon, VA / Hybrid or Remote

About the Role
VivSoft Technologies is scaling rapidly, and we are looking for a Contracts Specialist who sees contracts not just as a compliance function, but as a lever for growth. You will own the full contract lifecycle across our federal contracts, task orders, and subcontracts, while also being a trusted partner to our Growth, Capture, and Pricing teams during proposal development. This is a highly visible role in a company preparing for significant scale, and the person in this seat will directly shape how audit ready, deal ready, and growth ready our contracts function becomes over the next several years.

What You Will Do
Pre-Award (Presales and Capture Support)
  • Support the Growth and Capture teams by quickly executing NDAs and Teaming Agreements using our standard templates, distinguishing routine requests from those that need deeper review, so pursuits move fast without exposing VivSoft or our partners to unnecessary risk
  • Review solicitation terms and conditions during proposal development, flagging contractual risk and security requirements (including FCL/clearance requirements) before submission
  • Work closely with the Pricing team to ensure contract terms, subcontract flow downs, and risk allocation are properly reflected in pricing assumptions on complex bids

Post-Award (Contract Administration and Execution)
  • Administer the full post award contract lifecycle: negotiate, execute, and modify prime contracts, task orders, and subcontracts across FAR/DFARS based vehicles, FAR/DFARS-based vehicles (e.g., IDIQs, BPAs) and non-FAR instruments (e.g., OTAs)
  • Ensure contract compliance with FAR, DFARS, and agency specific supplements, and maintain clean, audit ready contract files in support of DCAA and other compliance reviews
  • Manage contract closeouts, options exercises, and modifications in a way that protects margin and reduces administrative risk
  • Maintain organized, defensible contract documentation that would hold up under any kind of audit
  • Coordinate with outside vendors to help establish and grow VivSoft's contracts function, developing documentation and standards of practice that support scalability.
  • Monitor and track key contract dates, deliverables, and reporting requirements and other contractual milestones proactively, so nothing slips and nothing surprises Delivery or Finance
  • Manage and maintain the Unanet Contract Management module, including contract, task order, funding, and subcontract information.

What We Are Looking For
  • 5+ years of federal contracts administration experience, including FAR/DFARS-governed contract vehicles (e.g., IDIQs, BPAs) as well as non-FAR instruments such as Other Transaction Agreements (OTAs).
  • Preferred certifications: CPCM, CFCM, CGCO, CPA, CGAP, PMP, CPSM, Lean Six Sigma.
  • Strong understanding of contract types, IDIQ, OTAs, FFP, T&M, cost reimbursable, and how contract structure affects risk and margin
  • Experience with federal contract systems such as SAM.gov, FedConnect,ESRS, and WAWF
  • Experience supporting or working closely with capture, proposal, and pricing teams, someone who can read an RFP and immediately see the contracting implications, not just administer what has already been signed
  • Comfort operating in a growing, fast-moving company where processes are still being built, not just maintained
  • Sharp attention to documentation and recordkeeping discipline, DCAA audit experience or exposure is a strong plus
  • Excellent communication skills, able to explain contract risk and terms clearly to non-contracts stakeholders across Delivery, Finance, and Growth
  • A genuine interest in growing with the company, this role has a clear path toward a more senior contracts leadership position as VivSoft scales

Why This Role Matters Right Now
VivSoft is on a clear growth trajectory, and how well we manage our contracts today directly shapes our competitiveness on future pursuits.. This is not a back-office paperwork role. It is a seat at the table for someone who wants their contracts expertise to actively shape how we win, how we deliver, and how we are positioned for the future

Salary: $100,000 - $140,000 depends on experience

Obsidian Security is the leading SaaS security platform, trusted by global enterprises like Snowflake, T-Mobile, and Algolia. We protect 200+ organizations across North America, Europe, the Middle East, Southeast Asia, Australia, and New Zealand, including many of the world’s largest Fortune 1000 and Global 2000 companies.

Founded in 2017 and backed by top investors like Greylock, Obsidian was built to close a critical gap: securing SaaS apps where business happens—Microsoft 365, Salesforce, and hundreds more. The company does this by offering a complete SaaS security platform to reduce risk, detect and respond to threats, and prevent breaches at the source. Obsidian was built by leaders who redefined endpoint and identity security at CrowdStrike, Okta, Cylance, and Carbon Black. Now, they’re transforming how SaaS is secured.

With AI driving rapid SaaS growth and complexity, agentic AI tools gain privileged access to sensitive data through integrations, creating new risks most security tools miss. Obsidian uniquely detects anomalous OAuth token activity and manages integration risks. Major announcements are on the horizon. Recognizing that SaaS security needs to evolve, Obsidian enables growing organizations to start with a lightweight, prevention-focused browser extension and expand coverage over time.

With global momentum, a growing partner ecosystem including SentinelOne, Databricks, and Google Cloud, and a major fundraise ahead, Obsidian is scaling rapidly toward long-term growth and IPO readiness.

About the role

Obsidian Security protects organizations against threats across their SaaS and identity environments. As we scale, we are deliberately rethinking how technical support is delivered. We are not looking to grow this function by adding headcount in proportion to ticket volume. We are looking to scale it through systems, automation, and agentic AI.

This role owns that transition. You will re-architect the support operating model around technology to resolve the majority of customer issues through automated and agentic systems rather than human effort. Traditional people-management experience is welcome, but is not what we are optimizing for. We are looking for an operator who has already built and run technology-led support at scale.

What you'll do

  • Own the support operating model and redesign it around automation and agentic AI rather than linear headcount growth.
  • Design, deploy, and continuously improve agentic support systems across the full lifecycle: triage, resolution, escalation, and follow-up.
  • Build the knowledge and data infrastructure these systems depend on, including knowledge bases, retrieval systems, and the telemetry that feeds them.
  • Define and instrument the metrics that prove the model works: deflection rate, automated resolution rate, cost-to-serve, time-to-resolution, and CSAT.
  • Integrate support tooling with the product, internal systems, and customer telemetry so that resolution becomes increasingly automated over time.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering to convert recurring support signals into product fixes and self-service capabilities.
  • Maintain support quality and SLAs for a technical cybersecurity customer base throughout the transition.
  • Lead a small, high-leverage team of support and automation engineers, hiring for technical and systems capability.

What we're looking for

  • A demonstrated track record of operationalizing agentic AI or automation in a technical support environment, with measurable deflection and cost-to-serve outcomes.
  • A strong systems and engineering orientation. You are comfortable with APIs, integrations, data pipelines, LLM-based tooling, and support platform configuration.
  • Experience supporting a technical B2B SaaS product. Cybersecurity, identity, or SaaS security context is strongly preferred.
  • Fluency in support of economics and the metrics that govern cost-to-serve and scale.
  • The ability to own and execute the technical roadmap for the support function end-to-end.

What this role is not

This is not a traditional people-management or org-scaling role. We are explicitly optimizing for someone who scales the function through systems and automation rather than linear headcount growth. The role has full autonomy to add headcount, but the purpose of that headcount is to improve the strategic delivery of the support model and to handle tier-three escalation management, not to absorb ticket volume. Conventional support-leadership experience is valued but secondary to demonstrated technical and automation capability.

Nice to have

  • Direct experience building or integrating LLM and agent frameworks.
  • Prior hands-on support engineering experience in a security or infrastructure product.

About the Program:

Every year, we sponsor 2 remote UX apprentices from anywhere in the world to join us for 7 months, either in the fall or spring seasons or online. Our UX apprentices work through the end-to-end UX design and UX research process for a startup idea of their choice that will help them attract hiring managers in that topic space or industry.
Apprentices take our program for free and receive 1:1 mentorship throughout the 7-month program. Alumni UX apprentices go on to make between $85,000 -$130,000 in UX design, product design, UX research, or service design roles after they complete the program.
We are committed to helping women, immigrants, POC, and LGBTQ folks break into tech and land 6-figure UX jobs. We help you land 6-figure UX jobs or coach you till you get it.

Apprenticeship Requirements:

This apprenticeship program is open to new grads and UX career changers alike! Here are some apprenticeship requirements to keep in mind before applying:
Interested in creative tech career paths in UX research, UX design, product design or service design
Willing to commit 5-10 hours of work per week to complete program deliverables
Willing to attend 2-3 hour weekend lectures to learn the end-to-end design process OR willing to complete online video course modules
Open to feedback from UX mentors and demonstrates a willingness to revise design work

Apprenticeship Program Learnings:

Build digital products and services 0-1
Lead end-to-end design process for a startup idea or topic of your choice
Lead product scoping and feature scoping, as well as entire project management
Identify target market for product and position product for launch success
Develop a business model for the product or service and demonstrate how the product/service will scale as the business model scales
Lead discovery research by managing user recruitment, creating research plans, writing interview guides, leading 8-16 discovery interviews, and synthesizing interview insights
Deliver a compelling UX design and business pitch for your startup idea, showcasing both qualitative and quantitative data to justify the problem space and the solution
Tell a compelling story about users by showcasing user types, personas, stakeholder maps, journey maps, process maps, service blueprints, ideation matrixes, sketches, wireframes, UX workflows, prototypes and other visual deliverables
Lead user testing of wireframes and prototypes to improve product/service usability and constantly iterate on your startup idea
Design a unique design system for your solution from scratch, creating components, a style guide, and branding for your solution
Analyze direct and indirect competitors to clearly articulate your solution’s differentiators and why your solution is innovative and more likely to succeed over competing options
Consult with startups to create a scope of work and fulfill UX research, UX design, product design and service design work based on your scope of work.

How to Apply:

The application takes a few minutes to complete and will ask you to send in your resume. You do NOT need to have a UX resume or portfolio to apply- we consider folks who are at the very beginning of their career change, who are still exploring multiple career options.
You will receive UX tips and challenges via email to help you with your transition into UX and will be contacted by us if you are being considered for the apprentice program. Once contacted, you will go through a brief interview process before joining the cohort. Due to the large volume of applicants, we cannot contact all applicants about their application status. jobs.description:
Our Purpose

At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.

About Us

SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.

Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

What Are We Looking For?

We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.

As a Sr. GTM Engineer, Outbound, you will be tasked with building the AI agents, automations, and integrations that speed up prospecting, sharpen targeting, and surface the signals reps need to close, embedded with the SDR and AE organizations. Success is measured in more qualified pipeline per rep, faster deal cycles, and reps who no longer do the manual version of this work. This is a senior individual contributor role where your leverage comes from what you ship, not from managing headcount, and you will set the craft bar for outbound automation and coach SDRs and AEs as you go.

What Will You Do?

Primary responsibilities include:

  • Automate prospecting by building agents that research accounts, build lists, and draft personalized outreach at scale for SDRs.
  • Build sequencing intelligence, designing workflows that optimize send times, cadence steps, and messaging based on engagement data.
  • Surface deal signals by building agents that mine call recordings and CRM activity for risk flags, buying signals, and next-best-action recommendations for AEs.
  • Own the outbound stack, integrating sales engagement, conversation intelligence, enrichment, and CRM so rep-facing data stays accurate and actionable, for example Outreach/Salesloft, Gong/Chorus, Salesforce, and ZoomInfo/Clearbit.
  • Support forecasting and pipeline hygiene by building automations that flag stale deals, missing data, and forecast risk before they become surprises.
  • Make quality measurable by building evals for outreach personalization quality, call-summary accuracy, and signal precision against human baselines.
  • Build the guardrails, implementing human-in-the-loop review for anything rep- or customer-facing, plus logging and rollback paths.
  • Coach and document, bringing SDRs, AEs, and revenue operations up the AI curve and building playbooks and reusable templates.
  • Ramp through a staged first year: in months 1 to 3, embed with one or two priority teams, map the current outbound motion end-to-end across prospecting, sequencing, call review, and deal progression, and ship your first prospecting or sequencing automation with an eval harness behind it; in months 4 to 6, deploy a deal-signal or call-intelligence agent live for AEs and stand up shared templates for outreach, personalization, and account research.
  • In months 7 to 12, own a meaningful slice of the outbound automation layer, show measurable gains in pipeline per rep, cycle time, and forecast accuracy, and hand off matured systems to SDR and AE leadership so they run day-to-day on the systems you built and instrumented.

What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?

Ideal candidates will have:

  • 6 or more years across sales development, sales operations, revenue operations, or systems/solutions engineering, with hands-on time building automation or AI into outbound or sales workflows.
  • Demonstrated experience designing, building, and deploying AI agents (prospecting agents, call-summary agents, deal-signal agents) that changed real pipeline or cycle-time outcomes.
  • Fluency with the outbound stack and how rep-facing data moves through it, including sales engagement platforms such as Outreach and Salesloft; conversation intelligence such as Gong and Chorus; CRM in Salesforce; forecasting in Clari; enrichment and prospecting through ZoomInfo, Clearbit, and LinkedIn Sales Navigator; and meeting scheduling through Chili Piper.
  • Strong prompt architecture skills and practical experience with agent frameworks, orchestration platforms such as n8n and Make, and API/MCP integrations.
  • Working proficiency in at least one of SQL, Python, or JavaScript, enough to build lightweight tools, integrations, and workflows.
  • A builder's instinct paired with GTM judgment: you understand quota, pipeline coverage, and deal stages, and you prioritize by revenue impact.
  • Experience building evaluation frameworks for AI systems (prompt evals, benchmarking, regression testing), and practical experience fine-tuning or heavily customizing models for production use cases, is preferred.
  • Familiarity with forecasting methodologies and pipeline hygiene practices is preferred.
  • Comfort coaching non-technical teammates through AI adoption and anticipating resistance without relying on positional authority is preferred.
  • A B2B or enterprise SaaS background, including familiarity with brand-safety and compliance constraints on automated outputs, is preferred.

Why SentinelOne?

AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment. From day one, we architected an AI-native platform designed to operate at machine speed, not as an add-on to legacy systems but as the foundation itself. If you want to build where innovation and impact move together, this is that place.

We invest in our Sentinels with comprehensive, competitive benefits designed to support you and your family:

Work Perks & Flexibility

Wellness & Lifestyle

  • Adoption & surrogacy reimbursement

We're transforming the grocery industry

At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers.

Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table.

Instacart is a Flex First team

There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work.

Overview

Instacart's mission is to create a world where everyone has access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Online Grocery is the heart of that mission — the products millions of customers rely on every day and the team that builds them. We're looking for a Chief of Staff, Online Grocery to partner with the General Manager who leads this business and its product and R&D organization of ~200 people across product, design, research and technical program management.

People, operations and programs are the core of the work — but what should energize you is what that work makes possible. A Chief of Staff here helps the organization operate at its best: more cohesive, clearer in its purpose, sharper and faster in how it makes decisions and operates, and enabled to do the thing that matters most — building products our customers love. If you're motivated by improving how a team works, and serve as a multiplier on everything the team can ship, this is your role.

This is a highly strategic and operational individual-contributor role (no direct reports) for someone exceptionally organized, has strong business and strategic sense, high in empathy, and who has an understanding of how product, design, and engineering teams work.

About the Job

Run the operating rhythm

  • Own and continuously improve the business rhythm for the GM and the organization — leadership team syncs, all-team meetings, monthly and quarterly business reviews, planning reviews, organizational communications, and Online Grocery segments of company-wide all-hands.
  • Manage the operating cadence for the GM — prioritizing and delegating workstreams, ensuring the right things get the right attention at the right time.
  • Improve how the organization decides: clarify decision rights and the questions that matter, build the frameworks and pre-reads that bring options into focus, and remove the friction that slows good calls.
  • Once decisions are made, capture and sharpen them, ensure they're communicated to the right stakeholders, and close the loop on execution — keeping leadership priorities, decisions, and commitments visible and on track (R&D execution itself is owned by TPM).
  • Shape and run the substance of the leadership team offsites: objectives, agenda, pre-reads, the hard discussions, decisions, and follow-through (logistics and events are handled separately).
  • Be a trusted thought partner to the GM and a credible problem-solving partner to product and R&D leaders, and build strong relationships with chiefs of staff across the organization to partner effectively in getting your responsibilities done.
  • Prepare briefings and coordinate research for the GM's meetings with partners and key leaders — identifying goals, talking points, and relevant context.
  • Partner with the GM, HR and finance to manage the organization's headcount budget

Plan executive communication

  • Drive the calendar, planning, and content for upward communication and alignment with the C-suite and the board on Online Grocery priorities.
  • Support the GM in preparing content for speaking engagements (working with our comms team).

Strengthen people, culture, and organizational health

  • Help the GM spot, diagnose, and get ahead of issues across the organization — bringing structured, candid read-outs and early signals, not just status.
  • Partner with the GM and HR to address relationship and culture dynamics across the team and create a high-trust, high-performance leadership team culture.
  • Turn signals like engagement surveys into action — working across the organization to develop the right plans, pressure-test them, and ensure they get executed and the loop gets closed with teams.

Drive priority programs

  • Help the GM kick off and drive annual and long-range planning for Online Grocery.
  • Take ambiguous new efforts for the GM from unclear to fully underway — creating clarity and a plan, identifying DRIs, setting up the decisions that need to be made, aligning stakeholders, and developing the right operating rhythm to track progress.
  • Proactively identify and take ownership of emerging opportunities and risks before they become blockers.

About You

Minimum Qualifications

  • 10+ years of work experience
  • R&D experience — earned in a direct R&D role (product, design, engineering, or technical program management), an adjacent role embedded with R&D teams, or as a Chief of Staff within an R&D organization
  • Consulting, corporate strategy/operations, or finance background and experience working directly with executives
  • Working fluency to navigate a product, design, and engineering organization at scale, and to be a true problem-solving partner to R&D leaders rather than a coordinator.
  • High EQ and a genuinely people-oriented instinct — builds trusted relationships, reads organizational dynamics, and bridges leadership and teams.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication at an executive level
  • Strong analytical skills, and a commitment to consistently high-quality work.
  • Exceptional program management: organized, effective, and relentless at driving multiple hard initiatives forward to deadline at once.
  • Ability to travel 10%

Preferred Experience

  • Experience designing and facilitating leadership offsites and driving organizational, culture, or operating-model change.
  • Experience building with AI (e.g., prototypes, automations, or agents) in a professional setting.
  • Experience within high-growth, technology-driven companies.

In 1968, the New York Stock Exchange began closing on Wednesdays so brokerage firms could catch up on paperwork. Every transaction depended on physical stock certificates being delivered, recorded, and reconciled. Trading had outgrown the infrastructure behind it. The expression “Paperwork crisis” had entered the nation's agenda resulting in other temporary measures like shortened trading days and extending settlement. The industry responded with electronic clearing systems and the establishment of the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) laying the foundation for markets that could operate at an entirely different scale.

Every share needs an identity, every movement needs a record, and every balance needs to agree with the institutions holding the assets. The best financial infrastructure makes this complexity feel ordinary. Building it takes extraordinary care.

At Mercury, our Investments team helps founders put their capital to work through products like Treasury and Invest. Our Custody team builds the systems underneath that experience: the ledger, security master service, reconciliation, and operational tools that keep customer assets accurately accounted for and give our products a dependable foundation to grow.

We’re looking for a senior engineering manager to lead the Custody team through its next stages of growth and scale to better serve our small and large customers.

As part of this role, you will:

  • Lead, hire, and develop a team of senior engineers, providing thoughtful feedback and building a trusting and supportive environment.
  • Own the team’s technical strategy and roadmap, translating Mercury’s investment ambitions into focused priorities and predictable delivery.
  • Guide the design and evolution of core custody systems, including cash and securities ledgers, security master service, position tracking, and reconciliation.
  • Partner with product, investment operations, and compliance to turn business and regulatory requirements into well-designed systems, operational controls, and auditable workflows that balance correctness, scale, and maintainability.
  • Collaborate with Product and Partnerships to align integrations, responsibilities, and technical roadmaps.
  • Set a high bar for correctness, reliability, and incident response, balancing new capabilities with the maintenance and improvement of critical systems.

The ideal candidate for the role:

  • Has 3+ years of experience managing highly technical teams.
  • Has direct experience building or operating RIA and broker-dealer custody systems at scale, including ledgers, security master service, cash and securities reconciliation, and money movement.
  • Understands the broker-dealer operating model and how responsibilities and data flow across introducing brokers, clearing firms, and custodians.
  • Has worked closely with compliance and operations teams, translating requirements into practical engineering decisions and effective controls.
  • Understands the lifecycle of securities and the implications of settlement and corporate actions for customer cash and positions across equities, fixed income, ETFs, and mutual funds.

A US-based telehealth mental health practice is looking for a Senior Director, Clinician Operations to own the non-clinical operations that support therapists from hire through onboarding, caseload growth, and offboarding.

The practice runs fully online with 100+ clinicians delivering around 7,000 therapy sessions a month, and is scaling toward 300+ clinicians while expanding into new states and adding new services. This is a build role: the seat reports to the COO and is responsible for the team, systems, and scorecards that make that growth possible, not for maintaining what already exists.

Day-to-day, this role runs clinician lifecycle operations, support and escalation workflows, capacity and caseload planning, and the reporting layer that tracks it all. It works across recruiting, credentialing, intake, scheduling, people operations, and revenue cycle without owning those functions, and it does not provide clinical supervision or make treatment decisions.   • Build onboarding playbooks and SOPs that hold up as headcount scales past 300.

Support & Escalation Management

  • Run intake, triage, and escalation workflows for a high-volume clinician support function.

  • Manage backlog and aging metrics to keep queues within target.

Performance & Metrics Ownership

  • Own operational KPIs including service levels, resolution times, productivity, and clinician retention.

Team Building & Leadership

Systems, Data & Automation

  • Since 2018, Juno has helped 290k+ students and families access over $2B in funding at the lowest rates available.
  • In 2025, we estimate 14–15% of all private in‑school graduate lending flowed through Juno and are growing rapidly;

We are the most popular way to find a private student loan for the world's top graduate programs, and we're looking for a team to help the financial aid offices understand the value we bring to students and families.

The Problem

Federal lending reforms have created a significant market shift. In July 2026, new caps on federal graduate loans, including the elimination of Grad PLUS for new students, came into effect, leaving millions of students with significant funding gaps. Students need transparent, competitive private options — exactly what Juno provides.

When a student hits that gap, they may ask a financial aid administrator. If that administrator has never heard of Juno, the student may never hear about us either.

Your mission

We're seeking up to fourteen Regional Directors, each owning one territory. Your job is to (i) ensure the administrators are aware about Juno, (ii) trust Juno enough that their students are also made aware about Juno (through numerous means such as direct mention by an administrator, getting Juno listed as a resource on a school's website, into a school's webinar calendar, and/or admitted student and current student communications). We expect you to thoroughly evaluate Juno to ensure you understand us deeply, so you can answer any questions about Juno, how we operate and the outcomes our members have.

What you'll do

  • Own a territory: Every financial aid office in it, and every relationship inside those offices. You build the plan, set the calendar, manage your budget and deliver results.
  • Build Relationships: Juno has tremendous value to add in the form of financial education and better loan products. Our model is different and we are not a lender. It can take time to gain full understanding and buy-in from the financial aid community. Keep showing up as a trustworthy voice.
  • Live in your associations: Membership, exhibiting, sessions, listservs, volunteer roles. This profession decides who's credible in person.
  • Get on campus: Conferences introduce; visits close. Six to eight campus swings a year.
  • Deliver webinars: Deliver institutional sessions from the standard deck. You don't have to write it, but you do have to practice it and run it like you did.
  • Keep your CRM true: Named contact, last touch, next step, on every active account. If it isn't in the CRM, it didn't happen.
  • Feed intel back: What competitors are offering, what's changing on campus, what students are actually asking. Product and marketing need it to help you succeed

Support our members: During peak borrowing season it’s all-hands-on-deck to ensure Juno members receive timely answers, 1:1 support, and the best customer service in the sector! You’ll likely be tapped to support member communications during peak.

  • Use AI as a multiplier: Institution research, RFI drafts, call prep, follow-up. Faster work, and you catch it when it's wrong.

What We Offer

Compensation: $115,000 plus $50k on-target bonus based on measurable, achievable outcomes.

Benefits: Comprehensive health, dental, vision, and 401(k) matching.

What We're Looking For

  • Background: 3+ years in financial aid administration, student lending sales, higher education partnerships, or a closely related role serving students. Having strong relationships within the financial aid/higher education sector is a must. Time in a financial aid office is valuable.

Ability to Prioritize: Understand where to focus your time and energy.

  • Consultative patience: A listing / webinar etc. can take several touches and time to establish trust.
  • You can present: To a room of aid administrators and to a room of students, on the same trip.
  • You can write: RFI and RFP responses are how schools judge whether we're serious.
  • Regulatory literacy: You can answer compliance and regulation questions accurately in the room without overpromising, and you escalate rather than improvise. We'll train you; you have to want to know.
  • Self-management: You build your own plan across dozens of institutions with no daily supervision, and you're honest in your own pipeline.
  • Curiosity about the product: You want to understand how student lending actually works — federal versus private, what drives a rate, cosigners, deferral, refinancing — because you can't advise an aid officer on a product you don't understand.
  • Comfort with seasonality: Fall and spring decide the year. You plan for them months ahead and go all-in when they land.
  • Location and travel: You live in your territory. Roughly 30% travel estimated (more or less depends on your execution), concentrated in those two seasons.

The X-Factor

  • You're the person they call: Aid officers ask your opinion on things you're not selling.
  • You're curious about the data: When a school says yes, your first instinct is to ask why — and whether the next school looks like it.
  • You close the loop: A campus visit isn't done until the notes are in the CRM and the next step has a date.
  • You're comfortable alone: You're the only Juno person in the building, and that's the part you like.

Why Join Juno?

The Opportunity

  • Real Impact: Help hundreds of thousands of students get access to the lowest rates on the market.
  • Market Timing: Federal aid changes create massive tailwind for growth.
  • Proven Model: $2B+ negotiated, 290K+ members.
  • Ground Floor: All new initiative. In most cases, you'll be the first Juno person your schools ever meet.

jobs.excerpt: RoleOwn the Salesforce to SAP integration for an order management build at a beverage manufacturer.
jobs.description:
Role

Own the Salesforce to SAP integration for an order management build at a beverage manufacturer. You run a two-week solution discovery with the client's IT team, agree the interface contract, then design and lead the integration through five build sprints to a February go-live. You are the senior technical voice on the integration and you write the specification the client's SAP team builds against.

What you will do

  • Agree an interface contract with the client's IT team covering the SAP services to be consumed, payload structures, error semantics, idempotency handling and retry behaviour.
  • Design inbound synchronisation of order header and line records from SAP into Salesforce over SAP Integration Suite.
  • Design write-back into SAP of order amendments, cancellations and return authorisations, including the reason codes recorded against each.
  • Design write-back integrity: validation, exception handling and reconciliation controls for failed, partial and duplicate transactions, a reconciliation record for every instruction originating in Salesforce, and a concurrency control that re-reads order state from SAP immediately before submission.
  • Establish during discovery the SAP services available, the SAP release in use, the order state model, authorisation thresholds, and the volume and cut-off of historic order data.
  • Work inside an existing programme team alongside a US-based lead architect, in that programme's sprint ceremonies and testing cycle.

Essential

  • Eight to ten years in Salesforce, currently operating as a solution or technical architect.
  • Salesforce to SAP integration delivered end to end, including transactional write-back into SAP rather than read-only surfacing of SAP data.
  • Integration patterns for transactional systems: idempotency keys, correlation identifiers, retry and backoff, dead-letter handling, and reconciliation between two systems of record.
  • SAP sales order interfaces for create, change and cancel, across both BAPI over RFC and OData. The client's SAP release is not yet confirmed, so both are required.
  • Salesforce integration mechanics: Apex callouts, named credentials, platform events, External Services, and the Salesforce Order data model.
  • Able to write an interface specification precise enough for a third-party SAP team to build against, and to hold that conversation directly with the client.
  • Fluent English, working the programme's ceremonies with a US-based team.

Desirable

  • SAP Integration Suite, specifically Cloud Integration. This is the client's first use of the platform.
  • Salesforce Integration Architect certification.
  • Manufacturing, consumer packaged goods or food and beverage order-to-cash exposure.

jobs.excerpt: EMPLOYER IS A CONTRACTOR FOR THE U. S.  GOVERNMENT.
jobs.description:
EMPLOYER IS A CONTRACTOR FOR THE U.S. GOVERNMENT. THIS POSITION WILL REQUIRE U.S. CITIZENSHIP.

Role Description

This is a forward-deployed engineering role. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with mission heroes: the users, operators, and program engineers who run real workloads in real DoD environments. You'll be the person who takes UDS Data Capability from "deployable" to "running in production under classification." You will deploy, harden, integrate, and operate our data stack in the mission hero's environment, then carry what you learn back into the product so the next engagement is easier.

The scope of this work varies by engagement. Some programs require standing up a governed data platform to centralize sensor or operational data from known sources, where the problem is well-defined and the priority is building and shipping. Others involve consolidating data across hundreds of interconnected government systems of record with overlapping schemas, deeply interdependent data flows, and significant architectural complexity. You should be equally comfortable executing against a defined data problem and navigating ambiguity in a complex data landscape where the right approach isn't yet clear.

Forward-deployed means aligned with the mission hero, not always on a plane. Most of the work is remote. You'll travel to sites when the engagement calls for it: initial standup, integration work, incident response, training and knowledge transfer. The rest of the time, you'll be on a video call or in a shared chat with that same mission hero. The role is defined by the relationship with the mission hero, not by where you sit.

You are a data engineer who can own the full breadth of a data platform (storage, ingestion, streaming, governance, and access) and deliver working solutions in constrained, mission-critical environments. About 20% of your time, you'll also invest in the forward-deployed team itself, pairing with junior Data Engineer FDEs on hard problems and helping them develop the technical judgment that only comes from field experience.

Responsibilities

  • Deploy and harden UDS Data Capability in the mission hero's environment. Stand up the UDS Store (Iceberg, Rook/Ceph, pgvector, Postgres), wire up UDS Transit for air-gap data movement, configure UDS Govern policies (Pepr/Lula), and integrate UDS Connect (Strimzi/Kafka) where streaming or legacy connectors are required.
  • Own the integration with existing mission systems. Connect UDS Data Capability to legacy databases, flat-file drops, SOAP/REST endpoints, message buses, existing object storage, and identity providers (Keycloak, mission-side SSO). Prior experience integrating with these types of systems is more relevant than experience building on them.
  • Map and navigate complex data landscapes. Some engagements involve hundreds of interconnected systems of record with overlapping schemas and deeply interdependent data flows. You'll need to trace how data moves across systems, identify dependencies, and advise government stakeholders on consolidation and architecture decisions.
  • Build pipelines that move data through classification boundaries, including ingestion, transformation, catalog registration, model/dataset packaging via Zarf, cross-domain transit, and eventual consistency across DDIL conditions.
  • Establish data provenance, lineage, and governance practices. Track where data came from, how it transformed, and who can access it.
  • Operate what you deploy. Initial day-2 ownership includes capacity, performance, backup/restore (Velero), observability (Vector/Loki), incident response, and upgrade paths. Hand off to the mission hero's ops team once it's stable.
  • Generate accreditation artifacts, including STIG evidence, cATO documentation, FIPS validation notes, and policy mappings. You produce the evidence the mission hero's ISSM/ISSO needs to run this in IL4/IL5.
  • Be the voice of the mission hero back to product and engineering. File issues, write postmortems, propose operator improvements, and ensure field experience directly informs platform development.
  • Train and transfer. Leave the mission hero's team self-sufficient through runbooks, architecture docs, working sessions, and knowledge transfer.
  • Grow junior Data Engineer FDEs. Pair on hard problems, review integration designs before they reach the customer, and accelerate technical development across the team. This is a mentorship role, not a management one.

Preferred Locations: Colorado Springs, CO or Florida Space Coast (Cape Canaveral / Cocoa Beach / Melbourne). Remote candidates will be considered, but local presence is strongly preferred.

Travel Expectations: Candidates based in Colorado Springs or the Florida Space Coast can expect on-site presence 1-2 days per week. Remote candidates should expect to travel to the engagement site for approximately one week every 4-6 weeks.

The listed responsibilities are not exhaustive and additional responsibilities may be assigned based on the evolving needs of the organization. We are seeking a dynamic individual who is able to adapt and take on new responsibilities as they arise.

Required Qualifications

Data engineering breadth

  • Unstructured data at scale. Production experience storing and querying large unstructured datasets using data lake architectures. Spark strongly preferred.
  • Streaming & integration. Building and operating stream processing infrastructure (Kafka, Redpanda, Flink, or equivalent) and bridging data from heterogeneous sources into modern pipelines.
  • Data warehousing. Open-source data warehousing platform experience. These environments do not support proprietary platforms, so you need to be comfortable building without them.
  • Pipelines & orchestration. Airflow, Dagster, Argo Workflows, or similar. Comfort building, scheduling, monitoring, and recovering production data pipelines.
  • Data modeling & SQL. Fluent in SQL. Comfortable designing schemas for both analytical and operational workloads.

Open-source orientation. You are comfortable building on open-source tooling and contributing back to it.

What "forward-deployed" requires

  • U.S. citizenship and the ability to obtain and maintain a DoD security clearance. Clearance sponsorship available for the right candidate.
  • Comfort being the technical face of Defense Unicorns to a mission hero. Clear communication with both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Comfort with periodic on-site work, sometimes for days at a stretch, and equal comfort working remotely.
  • Bias toward delivery. Preference for shipping a working integration over perfecting a design that hasn't met a real workload.
  • Self-direction. You will encounter environments and problems that are not yet documented and will need to work through them independently.
  • Willingness to mentor junior engineers and help them build technical judgment through hands-on experience.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Data provenance, lineage, and governance. Experience with lineage tracking, data catalogs, provenance systems, or governance frameworks. Depth here will be weighted heavily.
  • DoD or defense program experience.
  • Active Secret clearance (or higher).
  • Lakehouse & storage: Apache Iceberg (or Delta/Hudi), object storage (Ceph/S3-compatible), Postgres (including extensions like pgvector), columnar/OLAP engines (Trino, DuckDB, ClickHouse, Spark SQL).
  • Change Data Capture: Debezium or similar CDC patterns.
  • Governance, catalog & access: REST catalogs (Iceberg REST, Polaris/Gravitino/Nessie family), ABAC/RBAC patterns, OIDC/OAuth, lineage and audit.
  • Kubernetes awareness. Deep K8s expertise is not required; general familiarity with deployments, operators, and how applications run on Kubernetes is valuable.
  • Linux fundamentals, container runtime behavior, networking, TLS, secrets management.
  • IaC (Terraform, Pulumi, or similar) and GitOps patterns (Flux, ArgoCD).
  • Familiarity with the CNCF ecosystem, including the distinction between foundation projects and single-vendor projects.
  • AI/ML awareness. General understanding of how data infrastructure supports model training, versioning, provenance, and AI operations.
  • Familiarity with Air Force or Space Force systems of record (e.g., MILPDS, ARMS) and how data flows between them.

You do not need to meet every preferred qualification. You do need to be credible across the core data engineering requirements.

jobs.description:
The work we do has an impact on millions of lives, and you can be a part of it.
We help protect our customers against life’s uncertainties. Regardless of where you work within the company, you’ll be helping provide protection and peace of mind when our customers need it most.
Protective is looking for Data Engineers to design, build, and operate production data pipelines on Voyager, our Databricks lakehouse on Azure. You will own the end-to-end flow of data through a medallion architecture — ingesting source data into the Bronze layer, applying cleansing, validation, and conformance in Silver, and publishing trusted, consumption-ready data products in Gold.

This role sits at the intersection of engineering, analytics, and platform operations. You will write production-grade Python and SQL, enforce data contracts, and help Protective treat data as a product with named owners and real consumers. You will be embedded on a delivery pod that owns its data products end to end, rather than servicing tickets from a queue.

On Voyager, the medallion layers are named Raw, Prep, and Prod. They map directly to Bronze, Silver, and Gold and are used interchangeably in this description.

Key Responsibilities

    • Design, develop, and maintain production data pipelines on Databricks using Python, SQL, Apache Spark, and Delta Lake.
    • Build Bronze-layer ingestion that reliably captures data from APIs, relational databases, flat files, cloud storage, and SaaS platforms — using dlt (dltHub) and Databricks-native ingestion where each fits — including incremental loading, pagination, watermarking, state management, and replay after failure.
    • Develop Silver-layer transformations in dbt and Python over Delta Lake that cleanse, standardize, type, deduplicate, validate, conform, and enrich data so that it is reusable across domains. A meaningful share of this role is making messy source data trustworthy.
    • Create Gold-layer data products: dimensional models, slowly changing dimensions, fact and bridge tables, aggregates, and serving tables aligned to how consumers actually query.
    • Produce and maintain the curated datasets ML engineering trains and serves models from — feature and training tables that are versioned and reproducible, not one-off extracts.
    • Author and maintain data contracts using the Open Data Contract Standard (ODCS) — schema with real semantics, named owner, known consumers, quality rules, and freshness expectations — and assess backward compatibility before every change.
    • Implement data quality as code: uniqueness and not-null on keys at minimum, plus referential, accepted-value, freshness, and custom business-rule tests, surfaced to producers and consumers rather than buried in logs.
    • Orchestrate ingestion and transformation as assets in Dagster, deployed to Dagster Cloud, and operate what you build across development, branch, and production deployments — schedules and sensors, asset dependencies, backfills, and run observability.
    • Apply governance through Unity Catalog — catalogs, schemas, external locations, grants, row- and column-level security, and lineage — and handle credentials through Azure Key Vault rather than in code.
    • Implement incremental and merge-based processing with Delta Lake (MERGE, schema evolution, time travel, OPTIMIZE) and tune Spark jobs, table layouts, and compute for performance and cost.
    • Troubleshoot production failures, data-quality issues, source-system changes, and late-arriving or duplicate data — including backfills and recovery — and take part in the pod’s on-call rotation for the pipelines it owns, with root-cause analysis that closes the gap rather than reopening the ticket.
    • Build and maintain CI/CD for data assets in Azure DevOps — automated tests and CI checks on dlt, dbt, and Dagster changes, promotion from development through branch deployments to production, and releases that are repeatable and auditable.
    • Instrument what you own for observability: freshness, volume, quality, latency, and cost, with alerting tied to the SLAs and SLOs your contract commits to instead of depending on someone noticing.
    • Work inside the platform’s control expectations — least-privilege access, secrets in Azure Key Vault, change management through pull request and pipeline, and audit evidence that falls out of the deployment path rather than being reconstructed later.
    • Participate in code review and document architecture, runbooks, and data products so others can discover, trust, and reuse them.
    • Work with data architects, analysts, product owners, and business stakeholders to translate requirements into maintainable data solutions.

Qualifications

    Required Qualifications


    • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or a related field; equivalent practical experience considered.
    • 3+ years building and supporting production data pipelines in a cloud data platform environment.
    • Strong hands-on Python and SQL. Both are used daily and neither substitutes for the other.
    • Hands-on experience with Databricks or a comparable Spark-based lakehouse, including Delta Lake tables, MERGE, and incremental load patterns.
    • Practical understanding of medallion / multi-layer lakehouse design, and the judgment to say what belongs in Bronze versus Silver versus Gold.
    • Experience ingesting data from APIs, relational databases, files, or SaaS applications, including the incremental and state-management problems that come with it.
    • Working knowledge of dimensional modeling — grain, keys, facts and dimensions, slowly changing dimensions — and of ELT design patterns and data quality practice.
    • Experience with orchestration and scheduling using Dagster, Databricks Workflows, Airflow, Azure Data Factory, or similar.
    • Git-based source control, pull request review, automated testing, and CI/CD as normal practice — Azure DevOps or comparable.
    • Experience troubleshooting production data failures, performance bottlenecks, and source-system changes.
    • Experience with pipeline monitoring and alerting, and a working understanding of what a freshness or quality SLA means once real consumers depend on it.
    • Ability to explain technical designs and trade-offs to both technical and non-technical partners.

    Preferred Qualifications


    • Databricks certification (Data Engineer Associate or Professional) or equivalent demonstrated depth.
    • Unity Catalog experience: catalogs, schemas, volumes, external locations, storage credentials, permissions, and lineage.
    • dbt on Databricks, or another transformation framework used alongside Spark.
    • Python-based modeling frameworks over Delta Lake, and experience implementing Type 2 history, surrogate keys, and merge strategies in code.
    • Experience with a declarative Python ingestion framework such as dlt (dltHub), Airbyte, Meltano, or Fivetran.
    • Dagster experience specifically, including assets, asset checks, sensors, schedules, and branch deployments.

Overview

Navitus Health Solutions is seeking a Consultant, Accreditation Compliance to join our team!

The Consultant, Accreditation Compliance is a key member of the Accreditation Quality Team and is responsible for supporting and maintaining accreditation programs across Navitus. This role ensures compliance with accreditation standards delegated to or supported by Navitus Health Solutions through oversight of reporting, analysis, audits, validation activities, and continuous quality improvement initiatives. This role serves as a subject matter expert on accreditation standards and processes and provides consultation, guidance, and education to associates, leaders, clients, and other stakeholders. The Consultant partners across the organization to support accreditation readiness, quality management activities, delegation oversight, performance improvement initiatives, and successful accreditation outcomes.

Is this you? Find out more below!

Responsibilities

How do I make an impact on my team?

  • Serve as a subject matter expert on accreditation standards, requirements, and interpretations; provide consultation, guidance, and training to associates, leaders, clients, consultants, and other stakeholders regarding accreditation expectations, compliance requirements, and best practices.
  • Evaluate organizational practices, processes, and controls against applicable accreditation standards and identify opportunities to strengthen compliance, quality outcomes, and operational effectiveness.
  • Serve as the primary liaison with accreditation organizations, consultants, and external stakeholders as appropriate, communicating accreditation updates, regulatory changes, and compliance requirements to support organizational readiness and ongoing compliance.
  • Manage the Navitus Quality Management Program, including facilitating quarterly meetings, maintaining program documentation, and collaborating with departments to monitor performance metrics associated with applicable accreditation standards (e.g. URAC PBM, NCQA, etc.).
  • Perform accreditation audits and assessments to evaluate compliance with applicable standards, identify performance gaps, and recommend corrective actions.
  • Evaluate and enhance audit methodologies, quality processes, and performance measurement tools to improve operational efficiency, accreditation readiness, and organizational outcomes.
  • Lead root cause analysis activities and partner with stakeholders to develop, implement, and monitor corrective action plans that address compliance risks and improve organizational performance.
  • Collect and analyze quantitative and qualitative data, identify trends, risks, and opportunities, and provide recommendations that support continuous improvement and accreditation readiness.
  • Develop, maintain, and continually improve documentation, strategies, processes, and objectives required to achieve and maintain accreditation and support client accreditation activities.
  • Provide information, consultation, and training on accreditation standards, quality management practices, and industry best practices to associates, clients, and other stakeholders.
  • Lead all aspects of accreditation surveys and reviews, including preparation, coordination, facilitation, communication, and follow-up activities necessary to maintain accreditation.
  • Participate in client meetings and accreditation activities, representing Navitus’ accreditation position and providing consultative support related to accreditation standards and compliance requirements.
  • Develop and maintain client specific delegation agreements in collaboration with current and future accredited health plan clients.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

What our team expects from you?

  • Bachelor’s degree required in Healthcare Administration, Quality Management, Business Administration, Public Health, Pharmacy, or a related field, or equivalent work experience, required.
  • 5+ years of experience in accreditation, compliance, quality management, or a related field required.
  • Experience with accreditation programs such as URAC, NCQA, or similar accreditation organizations required.
  • Experience interpreting and applying accreditation standards and leading accreditation readiness, survey preparation, audit, or compliance activities required.
  • Participate in, adhere to, and support compliance program objectives.
  • The ability to consistently interact cooperatively and respectfully with other employees.

What can you expect from Navitus?

  • Top of the industry benefits for Health, Dental, and Vision insurance
  • 20 days paid time off
  • 4 weeks paid parental leave
  • 9 paid holidays
  • 401K company match of up to 5% - No vesting requirement
  • Adoption Assistance Program
  • Flexible Spending Account
  • Educational Assistance Plan and Professional Membership assistance
  • Referral Bonus Program – up to $750!

About us:

Foodsmart is the leading Foodcare platform in the U.S., built to deliver nutrition-driven healthcare at scale. Powered by a national network of Registered Dietitians, Foodsmart combines personalized clinical nutrition care, behavior change tools, and food benefits to improve member health outcomes while lowering healthcare costs.

Our platform is designed to foster healthier food choices, drive lasting behavior change, and deliver sustainable health outcomes. Through our highly personalized, digital platform, we guide more than 3 million members—including those in employer-sponsored health plans, regional and national Medicaid managed care organizations, Medicare Advantage plans, and commercial insurers—on a tailored journey to eating well while saving time and money.

Foodsmart seamlessly integrates dietary assessments and nutrition counseling with online food ordering and cost-effective meal planning for the entire family, optimizing ingredients both at home and on the go. We partner with national and regional retailers across the U.S., many of whom accept SNAP/EBT, making healthier food more accessible. Additionally, we assist members with SNAP enrollment and management, providing tangible access to nutritious food. In 2024, Foodsmart secured a $200 million investment from TPG’s Rise Fund, which supports entrepreneurs dedicated to achieving the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals. This investment helps us expand our reach, particularly to low-income workers who are disproportionately affected by diet-related diseases.

At Foodsmart, our mission is to make nutritious food accessible and affordable for everyone, regardless of economic status. We are committed to a set of core values that shape our culture and work environment:

👥 Customer First - You start with the member and work backwards.

🚀 Make It Happen - You act with urgency, use data, and hold high standards.

🤝 One Team - You collaborate with respect and commit as a group.

Whether you're a dietitian, a commercial leader, or a technologist, working at Foodsmart means being part of a team that is passionate, supportive, and driven by a shared purpose. Join us in transforming the way people access and enjoy healthy food.

About the role:

As a Member Support Agent, you will provide direct live support for incoming member inquiries regarding services, eligibility, appointments, platform access, and food benefits, while assisting with elevated technical troubleshooting, provider coordination, and special operational projects. As a core member of our team, you will drive issue resolution with a strong sense of urgency while maintaining high personal accountability for protecting sensitive member information.
This is a part-time position requiring approximately 29 hours per week. This position will offer time off and is not eligible for health insurance benefits.

You will:

  • Serve as the first point of contact for all inbound member inquiries, greeting every caller empathetically and patiently.
  • Accurately document interactions and ongoing resolutions to ensure seamless follow-up.
  • Efficiently navigate internal FAQs, knowledge base documentation, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) to resolve member questions on the spot.
  • Document interactions and ongoing resolutions to ensure seamless follow-up.
  • Ensure member records are accurate and complete.
  • Multitask using internal tools and resources to perform real-time eligibility checks while delivering clear, empathetic benefits guidance to members.
  • Field questions about the purpose and importance of Telenutrition.
  • Match our members with the right dietitian and find appointment times that fit into their lives.
  • Assist members with troubleshooting platform and account issues and provide basic technology troubleshooting help.
  • Serve as a resource to troubleshoot, explain, and manage patient inquiries regarding incentive offerings in partnership with internal teams and external vendors.
  • Maintain a high level of personal accountability when handling sensitive and protected information.
  • Collaborate with peers, leaders, and other internal groups to find accurate solutions to complex problems.

You are:

  • A strong communicator, both orally and in writing, that can adjust your communication style and preferences to fit various situations.
  • A disciplined self-motivator: Capable of staying focused, managing your time, and hitting productivity goals in a fully remote environment without direct, in-person supervision.
  • An active digital communicator: Proactive about reaching out to teammates and leadership via approved communication methods when you have questions or need support.
  • Able to manage multiple ongoing tasks without missing deadlines or cutoffs.
  • Resilient, and capable of quickly adapting to changes in workflows and processes, and able to pivot seamlessly when new information is provided.
  • Able to navigate knowledge bases and multiple systems simultaneously while staying engaged in communication on live calls.
  • Experienced in solving complex problems that require critical thinking and resource navigation.
  • Both independently motivated and team-minded, allowing you to manage your own time and tasks to hit your own goals while also supporting your peers and seeking help when needed.
  • Detail oriented and committed to providing accurate and complete resolutions, and willing to take ownership and responsibility for maintaining these standards.
  • Goal oriented and able to push yourself to meet both metric and quality goals.
  • Comfortable with both giving and receiving feedback, both between you and leadership and in a peer-to-peer capacity.

You have:

  • Reliable high speed internet access with minimum speeds of roughly 100 Mbps download and 20 Mbps upload.
  • Prior remote experience (Highly Preferred): 1+ years of experience working successfully in a dedicated work-from-home or hybrid call-center environment.
  • The ability to communicate complex information concisely in writing.
  • Experience working with sensitive and protected information, including PII and PHI, and a basic understanding of HIPAA.
  • A completely private, secure, and quiet workspace.
  • Availability to work between Monday through Thursday from 11AM - 5:30PM PST and Friday from 11:30AM - 5PM PST. Availability until 8 PM PST a plus!

What success looks like:

  • Quality Assurance (QA): Maintaining a high QA score (e.g., 90%+) on recorded live calls and written documentation.
  • First Contact Resolution (FCR): Resolving escalations efficiently without unnecessary back-and-forth.
  • Schedule Adherence: Reliability in covering the critical Monday through Thursday from 11AM - 5:30PM PST and Friday from 11:30AM - 5PM PST PST shift window.

✅ Remote-First Company
